title: rerere: resolve a conflict once
summary: Let Git remember how you resolved a conflict and replay it the next time the same conflict appears.

steps.title: Reuse recorded resolution
body: Some conflicts come back: the same feature merged into `main` and into `release/3.2`, or a long branch rebased again and again.
**rerere** (reuse recorded resolution) remembers each resolution you commit and applies it the next time the same conflict shows up:
git merge feature/bulk           # conflict; you resolve it and commit: "Recorded resolution for 'src/Limits.cs'."
git merge feature/bulk           # "Resolved 'src/Limits.cs' using previous resolution."

The memory lives in `.git/rr-cache`. `git rerere diff` shows what it would apply; `git rerere forget src/Limits.cs` drops a wrong one. Set `rerere.autoUpdate true` to also stage the reused resolution.

steps.prompt: rerere replayed a resolution in your merge. Why does Git still stop with `src/Limits.cs` listed as unmerged?
options: By default it fixes the file but leaves staging to you, so you can check it first
rerere failed and you must resolve by hand
It only works during a rebase
The resolution is applied after you commit
steps.explain: The file already holds the recorded resolution; Git waits for your `git add` so a remembered mistake does not slip in unseen. `rerere.autoUpdate = true` stages it as well.

steps.title: The same conflict, twice
prompt: `feature/bulk` in `~/shop` must be merged into **both** `main` and `release/3.2`, and it conflicts with each in the same place: `MaxItems`.
1. Turn on rerere for this repository.
2. On `main`, merge `feature/bulk` and resolve the conflict: bulk wins, so the line is `    int MaxItems = 500; // bulk orders`. Commit with Git's default message.
3. On `release/3.2`, merge `feature/bulk` again and let rerere resolve it; stage and commit.

checks.name: rerere is on and remembered a resolution
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && test "$(git config rerere.enabled)" = true && test -n "$(ls .git/rr-cache 2>/dev/null)"
checks.fail: `git config rerere.enabled true` must be set **before** the first merge, so the resolution is recorded in `.git/rr-cache`.

checks.name: both branches have the merge, with 500
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && for b in main release/3.2; do git merge-base --is-ancestor feature/bulk $b && git show $b:src/Limits.cs | grep -qx '    int MaxItems = 500; // bulk orders' || exit 1; done
checks.fail: `main` and `release/3.2` should both contain the merge of `feature/bulk`, with `MaxItems = 500` and no markers.

checks.name: no merge in progress, clean tree
checks.fail: A merge is still in progress or files are left over.

hints: `git merge feature/bulk` on `main`, then `git checkout --theirs src/Limits.cs`, `git add src/Limits.cs`, `git commit --no-edit`: Git prints `Recorded resolution`.
`git switch release/3.2`, `git merge feature/bulk` says `Resolved ... using previous resolution`; then `git add src/Limits.cs` and `git commit --no-edit`.
steps.explain: rerere pays off most during long rebases ("rebase onto main every morning") and when the same fix goes to several release branches. Because it is keyed on the conflict text itself, a different conflict never gets a wrong old answer, but a wrong resolution you once committed will be replayed: `git rerere forget <path>` then.

steps.prompt: Match the command to what it does.
pairs: show the resolution rerere would apply
drop a recorded resolution that was wrong
show the merge base inside conflict markers
